messages:

Subject: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up (HIPAA/BAA/SOC2)

Hi Sarah / Jason —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Call highlights:
- You’re evaluating LLM-based clinical triage and patient messaging features that will process PHI (patient names, limited notes).
- Primary compliance requirements: HIPAA (BAA required), SOC 2 Type II evidence for vendor security posture, and an audit log retention window of 7 years for specific flows.
- Latency target: 100–200ms p95 for short-turn responses; throughput: ~50 qps baseline with spikes to 200 qps during peak hours.

Deployment options we discussed (brief):
1) Hosted API (fastest path, shared tenant) — simplest integration, but would require our HIPAA hosting add-on and an executed BAA; typically used when customers are comfortable with our hosted controls and SOC2 attestation.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) — provides stronger isolation, dedicated endpoints for predictable throughput and data controls; often used by customers who need throughput SLAs and stronger data separation but can still rely on Redwood-managed infra.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full customer network control; recommended for customers with very strict audit/networking requirements or when on-prem air-gapped deployments are mandated by policy.

Questions / ask from your side:
- Can you confirm whether Elara will sign a BAA?
- For SOC2, would a copy of our latest SOC2 Type II report suffice for your vendor assessment, or do you need additional evidence (penetration test reports, architecture diagrams, key management attestation)?
- Any internal constraints that would force a private/on-prem approach vs. dedicated? For example, ownership of keys (KMS/HSM), or data residency concerns?

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll attach our SOC2 Type II (2025) and a draft BAA for your legal team to review.
2) Marissa (cc) will scope a pricing estimate for both Dedicated and Private options based on your throughput numbers and retention needs.
3) If you’re open, propose a short follow-up next week to go over the BAA and mutual action plan.

Attachments: SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf (attached), BAA_draft_Elara_20260810.docx (attached)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the SOC2 report if helpful.

Best,

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Phone: +1 (415) 555-0147

Thanks, Dylan — great summary and appreciate the quick turnaround. A few notes from our side: 

- We do require a signed BAA to proceed; legal will do an initial review but confirming intent to sign is helpful.
- For SOC2, the Type II report is the primary artifact our security team uses. We may follow up with specific questions, and we sometimes request a short architecture diagram of where customer data is persisted (KV cache, logs) and whether keys are customer-managed.
- Regarding deployment: our default preference is Dedicated capacity if it meets cost targets — gives us the isolation we want while keeping Redwood as the operator. Private/VPC is possible but requires approval from infra and security (will add that to the internal review).

I’ve attached the SOC2 report from our call (SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf) that you shared — I scanned a copy for our procurement queue and uploaded to our vendor portal.

Next steps from Elara:
- Legal will review the BAA draft this week.
- Security will review the SOC2 and may send a short questionnaire (likely focused on key management and audit log retention).
- We should plan a follow-up next Tue/Wed to review their initial comments.

Thanks — Sarah

Appreciate the quick confirm, Sarah. 

A couple quick clarifications that should help your security team’s review: 
- Key management: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations and HSM-backed options for Dedicated/Private deployments. We’ll enumerate the options in the architecture diagram.
- Audit logs: We can provide configurable audit log retention up to 7 years for records that are required for compliance; standard retention is 90 days but adjustable for enterprise plans.
- Data persistence: By default, short-term KV cache is used for performance; persisted logs/metrics can be routed to customer destinations in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Marissa — tagging you to start a cost/ops estimate for: 
- Dedicated capacity (50 qps baseline, 200 qps peak, 7-year audit retention option)
- Private VPC/On-prem evaluation (high level, include expected lead times for on-prem packaging and any additional support costs)

Sarah — I’ll send a short mutual action plan with milestone dates (BAA review, security questionnaire, pricing) and propose Tue/11 Aug 10:00 AM PT for a 30-minute sync unless that doesn’t work for you.

Dylan
